latest_checked.claim: Slow-wave sleep will increase as training volume builds and adenosine accumulation rises

stance.headline_read: I remain cautious about deep sleep trend interpretation given early-window noise and the absence of the Zone 2 training driver I predicted would activate slow-wave increases. The recent downward refutation doesn't shift my core mechanistic read—I predicted upward movement contingent on structured adenosine accumulation that hasn't yet appeared in his logs, so the absence of that driver is more informative than the direction itself. My focus stays on protocol stability, protein intake stabilization, and waiting for the training data that would reshape architecture.

stage.label: Protocol stabilization, signal waiting
stage.rationale: Matthew is in a holding pattern after 38 days with high rapport but incomplete behavioral compliance on logging. The simplified protocol is now active but signal quality remains unproven. The deep sleep refutation is consistent with noise in the absence of the mechanistic driver (Zone 2 adenosine accumulation) I predicted would activate increases. He's waiting for the levers—protein intake sustained at threshold, structured training volume—to appear before architecture changes become interpretable.

stance.confidence_note: My general confidence remains low (0.2) reflecting the wide prediction intervals and unresolved device-subjective divergence. Sleep duration confidence is moderate (0.467) after the September 12 recalibration; recovery and HRV confidence are lower (0.444 and 0.667 respectively) due to refuted directional calls and the 16-day logging gap that blocks subjective validation. I am more confident in naming what I don't know than in claiming signal where noise remains plausible.

trait_scores.note: A careful reader of converging signals — quick to say she was wrong, slow to say she's sure.
